mergedParams.userDescription: Text appearing and disappearing with clean, precise cuts, no fades. typo kinetics for titles/captions/other text..

output.title: Sharp Cut Typography - Clean Text Animations

prompts.prompt: Create a typokinetics preset that mimics classic film title cards with hard cuts between text segments. Like a video editor creating a montage of title cards, each text element should appear instantly at full opacity (no fades) and disappear with a hard cut. Structure the text within centered BaseLayout containers using 'flex items-center justify-center h-full'. Each TextAtom should have precisely timed visibility using opacity keyframes that jump from 0 to 1 instantly (no easing). Think of this like cutting between title cards in a film reel - each text segment gets its own 'shot' with clean entry and exit points. For captions/subtitles, use the word-level timing data to create staccato appearances where each word appears with a hard cut, stays visible for its duration, then cuts to black before the next word appears. This creates a rhythmic, percussive reading experience similar to kinetic typography in music videos.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with containerProps.className='relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' as the main container. For each text segment, create a child BaseLayout with containerProps.className='absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center' and use TextAtom components. Implement hard cuts using generic effects with opacity keyframes: [{time: 0, value: 0}, {time: 0.001, value: 1}, {time: 0.999, value: 1}, {time: 1, value: 0}] with linear easing. For caption-based text, iterate through captionData.words array and create individual TextAtom components with relative timing based on word.relativeStart and word.relativeEnd. Set each word's duration precisely to create gaps between words. Use fitDurationTo: 'children' on parent containers to automatically adjust timing. Consider creating an internal effect preset called 'hard-cut' for reusability. Use will-change: opacity for performance optimization.

prompts.prompt: Design a typewriter-style typokinetics preset where text appears character by character with instant visibility (no fade), similar to command-line interfaces or retro computer terminals. As a video editor would create a typing effect by revealing characters frame by frame, implement this using CSS clip-path to reveal text progressively while maintaining hard edges. Each character should 'pop' into existence with mechanical precision. For titles, reveal the entire string character by character. For captions, process each word individually, typing them out in sequence with brief pauses between words. Add an optional blinking cursor that appears and disappears with hard cuts (no fade) at the end of each typed segment.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using containerProps.className='relative w-full h-full bg-black' for terminal aesthetic. Use TextAtom with monospace font (e.g., 'Courier New:400:normal'). Implement character reveal using generic effects with clipPath property: animate from 'inset(0 100% 0 0)' to 'inset(0 0 0 0)' with stepped timing (no easing between characters). Calculate timing based on text.length * characterDuration. For captions, use captionData.words array and apply typing effect to each word sequentially using word.relativeStart for timing offset. Create a separate BaseLayout with ShapeAtom for the cursor (a thin rectangle with className='w-0.5 h-6 bg-green-400') using opacity keyframes [0,1,0,1] for blinking effect. Use transform: translateZ(0) for GPU acceleration. Consider creating a 'typewriter-reveal' internal effect preset.

prompts.prompt: Build a glitch-text typokinetics preset inspired by digital corruption and video compression artifacts. Text should appear and disappear through instant digital 'glitches' - no smooth transitions. Like a video editor creating a datamosh effect, implement sudden position shifts, instant color channel separations, and hard cuts between normal and corrupted states. Text should 'glitch in' by instantly appearing with RGB channel separation, then snap to normal position, then 'glitch out' with another instant corruption before disappearing. For dynamic captions, apply glitch cuts to individual words, creating a fragmented, disrupted reading experience where words appear to break through digital noise.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use nested BaseLayout containers with containerProps.className='relative w-full h-full isolate'. Create three duplicate TextAtom components for RGB channel separation, each with mix-blend-mode (use containerProps.style for blend modes). Apply instant position shifts using translateX/translateY in generic effects with step timing: [{time: 0, value: -5}, {time: 0.1, value: 0}, {time: 0.9, value: 0}, {time: 1, value: 5}]. Use filter effects for instant color shifts: 'hue-rotate(120deg)' for red channel, 'hue-rotate(240deg)' for blue. Implement hard cuts with opacity: [0,1,1,0] with no easing. For captions, process captionData.words and apply random glitch offsets to each word's position. Use transform: translate3d() for hardware acceleration. Create internal effect presets: 'glitch-in', 'glitch-out', 'channel-shift'.

prompts.prompt: Create a cinema subtitle typokinetics preset that emulates professional film subtitling with instant appearance/disappearance. Like a video editor working with subtitle tracks, implement clean, readable text that appears exactly when needed and vanishes without transition. Focus on optimal readability with high contrast backgrounds that also cut in/out instantly. For multi-line captions, implement line-by-line reveals where each line appears as a hard cut, similar to how subtitles in foreign films handle longer dialogue. Include options for different subtitle positions (bottom, top, or following speaker position) with instant position changes when switching speakers.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using containerProps.className='absolute bottom-0 left-0 right-0 p-8' for standard subtitle positioning. Add a semi-transparent background using a child BaseLayout with className='bg-black/80 px-4 py-2 rounded' that appears/disappears with the text. Use TextAtom with readable sans-serif font ('Inter:500:normal') and className='text-white text-center'. For hard cuts, use opacity effects: [{time: 0, value: 0}, {time: 0.01, value: 1}, {time: 0.99, value: 1}, {time: 1, value: 0}]. Process captionData.sentences for line breaks, creating separate TextAtom components for each line with staggered timing if needed. For speaker changes, use translateY with instant jumps: [-100, 0] or [0, -100] for position switches. Implement fitDurationTo: 'media' to sync with video duration. Use pointer-events: none to prevent interaction blocking.

prompts.prompt: Develop a rhythmic typokinetics preset that treats text like percussion in a music video. Each word or phrase appears and disappears on the beat with zero fade time - pure hard cuts synchronized to rhythm. As a video editor would cut footage to match musical beats, implement text that 'hits' on specific beats and cuts away cleanly. For titles, break them into rhythmic chunks that appear in sequence. For captions with audio, use beat detection to time the hard cuts. Create a stroboscopic effect where text flashes in and out rapidly during intense sections, similar to how music videos use quick cuts during drops or choruses.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with containerProps.className='fixed inset-0 flex items-center justify-center'. Implement beat synchronization by fetching audio analysis data using props.fetcher. Map beat timestamps to text appearance using generic effects with instant opacity changes. For each beat, create keyframes: [{time: beatTime, value: 1}, {time: beatTime + 0.05, value: 0}]. Use captionData.words array and align word appearances to nearest beat timestamps. For strobe effects during intense sections (check audio intensity > threshold), create rapid opacity toggles: [1,0,1,0,1,0] over short durations. Consider using waveform effects with 'bass' or 'waveform' properties for audio-reactive scaling that snaps to values (no smooth transitions). Create internal effect presets: 'beat-cut', 'strobe-cut', 'rhythm-sync'. Use transform: scale3d() for GPU-accelerated scaling on beats.

prompts.prompt: Design a split-screen typokinetics preset inspired by comic book panels and split-screen editing techniques. Text appears in distinct rectangular zones that cut in and out instantly, like a video editor creating a multi-panel composition. Each text element occupies its own 'panel' with hard-edged boundaries. Panels appear and disappear with no transition - pure cuts. For longer captions, distribute words across multiple panels that appear in sequence or simultaneously. Create dynamic layouts where panels can appear in different configurations (2x2 grid, vertical strips, horizontal bands) with instant switches between layouts.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Create a grid structure using BaseLayout with containerProps.className='grid grid-cols-2 grid-rows-2 gap-1 w-full h-full'. Each panel is a child BaseLayout with className='relative overflow-hidden border-2 border-white'. Use TextAtom within each panel with className='flex items-center justify-center h-full p-4'. Implement instant visibility using opacity: [{time: 0, value: 0}, {time: 0.001, value: 1}] for appearance. For layout changes, use CSS Grid template areas or change grid-cols/grid-rows classes dynamically. Process captionData.words and distribute across panels using modulo operation for word index. Create variations with different grid configurations: 'grid-cols-3', 'grid-cols-1 grid-rows-3', etc. Use clip-path: polygon() for non-rectangular panels if needed. Consider sub-presets for different panel layouts: 'comic-2x2', 'comic-strips', 'comic-diagonal'.

prompts.prompt: Build a news ticker typokinetics preset that mimics broadcast news with instant text transitions. Like a video editor creating lower thirds and breaking news banners, implement text that slides in from off-screen but appears/disappears with hard cuts at the entry/exit points. The sliding motion should be smooth, but the visibility cuts should be instant. For titles, create bold headline treatments that slam into place. For continuous captions, implement a ticker tape effect where text scrolls horizontally but individual words cut in at the edge and cut out at the opposite edge, maintaining constant motion without fades.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with containerProps.className='absolute bottom-0 left-0 right-0 h-24 bg-red-600' for news banner aesthetic. Add a scrolling container with className='overflow-hidden relative h-full'. Implement horizontal scrolling using translateX animation from 100% to -100% of container width. For hard cuts at edges, combine with clipPath: 'inset(0 0 0 0)' to 'inset(0 -100% 0 100%)'. Use TextAtom with bold sans-serif ('Roboto:700:normal') and className='text-white text-2xl whitespace-nowrap'. For ticker effect, calculate total duration based on text length and scroll speed. Process captionData.words to create continuous text string with proper spacing. Add a second BaseLayout for the headline area with instant appearance using opacity [0,1]. Consider creating internal effects: 'ticker-scroll', 'slam-in'. Use will-change: transform for smooth scrolling performance.

prompts.prompt: Create a flashcard typokinetics preset that treats each text element like a physical card being flipped or swapped. As a video editor would cut between different cards in a deck, implement instant transitions where one text 'card' is immediately replaced by another. No crossfades - just hard cuts between cards. For educational captions or Q&A content, show question text on one 'card', then instantly flip to reveal the answer. Include variations where cards can slide in from different directions but always with instant appearance at the start position and instant disappearance at the end.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using containerProps.className='relative w-full h-full perspective-1000' for 3D card effects. Create card containers with className='absolute inset-4 bg-white rounded-lg shadow-2xl flex items-center justify-center p-8'. Use TextAtom with className='text-gray-800 text-center'. For instant card swaps, use opacity [1,0] on outgoing card and [0,1] on incoming card with minimal overlap (0.01s). For flip effects, combine rotateY (0deg to 180deg) with backface-visibility: hidden, but make the rotation instant at the midpoint. Process captionData for Q&A pairs, alternating between question and answer cards. For directional slides, use translateX/translateY with instant position changes: [-100%, 0] or [100%, 0]. Create internal effect presets: 'card-swap', 'card-flip', 'card-slide'. Use transform-style: preserve-3d for proper 3D rendering.

prompts.prompt: Develop a terminal-command typokinetics preset that simulates command-line output with instant text appearances. Like editing a screencast of terminal usage, each line of text appears instantly as if executed by a command. No typing animation - just immediate full-line appearances with hard cuts. For multi-line captions, treat each line as a separate command output that appears sequentially. Include prompt indicators (>, $, #) that appear instantly before each text line. Create an option for 'error' text that appears in red with instant color switches, simulating command failures or warnings.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with containerProps.className='bg-gray-900 p-4 font-mono overflow-auto h-full' for terminal appearance. Structure each line as a BaseLayout with className='flex items-start mb-1'. Add prompt TextAtom with className='text-green-400 mr-2' containing '>' or '$'. Main TextAtom uses className='text-gray-300 flex-1'. Implement instant line appearance using opacity: [{time: 0, value: 0}, {time: 0.001, value: 1}]. Process captionData.sentences to create separate lines, each appearing after previous line's duration. For errors, conditionally apply className='text-red-500' based on metadata. Calculate relative timing: each line starts at previous line's end + small gap (0.1s). Use fitDurationTo: 'children' on container. Consider sub-presets: 'terminal-prompt', 'terminal-output', 'terminal-error'. Add optional ShapeAtom cursor with className='inline-block w-2 h-4 bg-green-400 ml-1' with blinking opacity [1,0,1,0].

prompts.prompt: Design a billboard typokinetics preset inspired by urban LED displays and stadium scoreboards. Text appears and disappears through pixelated digital transitions - imagine each character made of LED pixels that switch on/off instantly. Like a video editor creating a jumbotron effect, implement text where individual 'pixels' or segments turn on simultaneously to form letters, then turn off as a unit. For animated captions, create a scanning effect where text is revealed in horizontal or vertical bands that cut in sequentially, similar to how LED displays refresh. Include options for different pixel densities and color modes (monochrome, full RGB).
prompts.technicalSpecs: Create pixelated effect using BaseLayout with containerProps.className='relative w-full h-full bg-black p-8'. Use CSS grid for pixel simulation: className='grid grid-cols-[repeat(auto-fill,minmax(4px,1fr))] gap-px'. For actual text, use TextAtom with large bold font ('Bebas Neue:400:normal') and apply a pixel filter effect using SVG filters or CSS image-rendering: pixelated. Implement instant on/off using opacity keyframes with no easing: [0,1] for on, [1,0] for off. For scanning reveal, use clipPath with horizontal bands: 'inset(0 0 100% 0)' to 'inset(0 0 0 0)' in steps. Process captionData.words and assign each to a display 'segment' with staggered instant appearances. Create internal effects: 'led-on', 'led-off', 'led-scan'. For RGB mode, layer three TextAtom components with red/green/blue filters using className='mix-blend-screen'. Use transform: translateZ(0) for compositing optimization.
